transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I suppose it’s mostly that my head has been feeling a bit foggy lately. I keep mixing up simple things—appointment times, dates for exhibits, and even which volunteer I already called. It’s probably not terrible, but it’s been enough that I thought I should come in and ask about it, if that makes sense.
How long have you been experiencing this foggy feeling in your head?

Oh, I’d say… about four months now, more or less. It seemed to start around when we had that water damage and the remodel got going. I thought it was just the disruption, you know, but it’s been hanging on a bit.
Have you noticed any difficulty remembering things that happened before the water damage and remodel?

I’m not sure it’s so much things from before, Doctor. What I’ve really noticed is more the everyday mix-ups lately—appointment times, exhibit dates, and whether I already called a certain volunteer. It’s embarrassing, but I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.
Do you ever feel unsure about where you are or what time of day it is?

No… I don’t think so, Doctor. I mean, I might lose track of the hour if I’m busy or distracted, but I know where I am. I haven’t had that feeling of not recognizing a place or anything like that, at least not that I’ve noticed.
Have you had trouble learning new things recently?

A little, yes… though I don’t want to overstate it. It’s more that my head feels foggy, and I mix up simple things I should be able to keep straight—like appointment times, exhibit dates, or whether I already called a volunteer. New things don’t seem to stick as easily as they used to, if that makes sense.
Do you ever feel disoriented or unsure about the current year or season?

No, I don’t think so. I know what year it is and what season we’re in… at least, I haven’t felt mixed up about that. If I pause, it’s usually just me thinking, not because I don’t know. Does that make sense?
Have you been having trouble finding the right words when you're talking or writing?

Sometimes, yes… not terribly, I don’t think, but my head feels foggy and I can lose what I’m trying to say. It’s more like I mix up simple things—appointment times, exhibit dates, or whether I already called a volunteer. I feel a little embarrassed about it, honestly. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Have you noticed any significant difficulty recalling important information or events from your past?

No, I don’t think so… not important things from long ago, anyway. I can remember the big events and people in my life. I might be slow pulling something up now and then, but I haven’t noticed losing whole pieces of my past or anything like that. Is that what you mean?
Do you have trouble focusing or paying attention to things?

Yes… somewhat. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but my head has been feeling foggy, and I do lose track of simple things. Like appointment times, or dates for exhibits, or whether I already called a certain volunteer. That’s actually part of why I came in. Is that what you mean by focusing?
Have you noticed any changes in your mood or personality lately?

A little, yes… though I don’t want to overstate it. When the house work first started, I felt almost wonderfully charged up, like I could take on everything. But I suppose I was more sharp with people than I meant to be. I’d snap at my husband, or at the young volunteers, if they questioned my plans. It wasn’t very like me, I don’t think… or at least I hope not. Is that the kind of change you’re asking about?
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately?

I’m not sure I’d call it a big change. I’ve had a few nights where I didn’t sleep as well, but at my age that doesn’t seem so unusual. I’m still getting to bed and all that. Do you mean trouble falling asleep, or waking up, or…?
Have you been feeling anxious lately?

Anxious… I don’t know. Maybe a little, but not in a way I’d want to make too much of. I suppose I’ve been more on edge with everything going on, but I wouldn’t say I’m terribly anxious. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Have you been feeling depressed lately?

Depressed? No… I don’t think so, not really. I mean, everyone has a low day now and then, especially when things are unsettled, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been depressed. Is that all right—does that answer what you mean?
Have you had any significant changes in your physical health recently?

Well… nothing major, I don’t think. I haven’t been sick exactly. I suppose my appetite hasn’t been wonderful—most days I just pick at a little toast or soup because food doesn’t sound very good. And my skirts have been a bit looser, though I wasn’t trying to lose weight. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been experiencing any hallucinations?
Hallucinations… no, I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed seeing or hearing things that aren’t there, at least not that I’m aware of. Is that what you mean?
Do you think your ability to think and make decisions has changed significantly over the past four months?

Yes… I suppose it has, though I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. What brought me in is that my head feels sort of foggy, and I keep mixing up simple things—appointment times, exhibit dates, and whether I already called a volunteer or not. Little things like that, but enough that it’s been worrying me. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have you ever felt like your confusion comes and goes throughout the day?

I’m not sure I’ve noticed it coming and going like that, no. It feels more like… I’ll realize after the fact that I’ve gotten something mixed up. I haven’t been keeping track of whether it’s worse at certain times of day. Should I be paying attention to that?
Does your confusion or foggy feeling seem to vary throughout the day?

I don’t know that it changes much during the day, honestly. It’s more that my head just feels foggy, and I keep mixing up simple things—like appointment times, dates for the exhibit, or which volunteer I already called. It’s embarrassing, but that’s really what made me come in.
Do you feel like your foggy feeling or confusion is getting worse over time?

I think… maybe a little, yes. Not suddenly, but enough that I finally thought I should ask someone. It’s mostly that foggy feeling and mixing up simple things—appointments, exhibit dates, whether I already called a volunteer. I don’t want to overstate it, but it does feel like it’s been happening more than it used to.
Have you experienced any traumatic events in the past four months?
No, I don’t think so… nothing I’d call traumatic, anyway. I mean, life has its normal stresses, but nothing in the last few months that stands out like that. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
